text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Namibian government plans to expropriate land from private owners who are either not utilising it properly or who are found to own too much. Minister of Lands, Resettlement and Rehabilitation, Pendukeni Ithana, said this would be done in accordance with the 1995 Argicultural Land Reform Act.
- A verbal attack on homosexuals by the ruling SWAPO party has provoked protest at home and abroad including from the U.S., Sweden and South Africa.
- The acquisition of agricultural land by government will in future not only be based on the "willing seller, willing buyer" concept.
- A new 98 km stretch of the Trans-Caprivi-Highway was officialy opened on Thursday. The newly tarred road is part of one of the most important infrastructural projects in Southern Africa.
